messages:
maya: Heads-up — ran a p95-focused run against the runway allocator this morning. Observed small tail spikes when route=interactive-high and sequence>1024.
sam: hmm, any obvious correlation with kernel swaps or kv cache churn?
maya: yes, saw a cluster of KV misses right before the spikes. trace attached in logs. Also kernel switch from fast-attn->fallback around the same time.
tony: can you paste the log snippet? curious about the timing relationship.
maya: ```
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] route=interactive-high seq=1200 kv_hit=false kernel=fallback latency=248ms
[2026-03-18T09:12:03Z] route=interactive-high batch_size=4 token_budget=320 p95_target=180ms
[2026-03-18T09:12:04Z] route=interactive-high kernel=fast-attn warmup=false latency=190ms
```
eli: looks like the allocator gave the route a 320-token runway which caused microbatches that triggered fallback kernels due to sequence length distribution. The KV misses probably amplified the tail.
nina: what was the queue admission policy during the run? FIFO, priority by tier, or token-aware?
maya: token-aware with soft-priority for premium routes. But the token accounting was per-route rather than per-tier, so noisy routes could blow their runway quickly.
tony: suggestion: move to a hierarchical runway — tier-level cap + per-route floor. That way a noisy route can't exhaust the whole tier budget.
sam: agree. Also consider prefetching likely KV keys for interactive-high based on recent prefixes — reduces misses during long sequences.
eli: small experiment idea: reduce per-route max runway from 320->220 and add a tier buffer of 500 tokens. Keep p95 target 180ms and throttle above 90% runway usage.
maya: I ran that as canary for one nodepool: p95 improved from 215ms->178ms for interactive-high, tail occurrence dropped 60%.
nina: nice. Any regression on cost? fewer microbatches -> less GPU kernel churn?
maya: cost delta negligible (+~0.3%) since we reduced some batching efficiency but avoided expensive fallback runs.
tony: cool. next steps: 1) formalize hierarchical runway config 2) add KV-prefetch heuristic for top 5 interactive routes 3) add metric alert for kernel-fallback-rate > 0.5%/min.
sam: +1. Also add a small change to the token-accounting window (from 1s->200ms) so runway reflects recent bursts instead of a 1s averaged view.
maya: ticketed: INF-3247 for config + canary plan, INF-3248 for kv-prefetch spike script, INF-3249 for alerting. I'll schedule a canary tonight.
ci-bot: deploy-bot: Canary deployment queued — infra/canary-runway-adjustment -> scheduled at 2026-03-18T23:00Z :rocket:
maya: thanks — will post results in morning. if anyone wants to review the trace I pushed a link: https://internal.redwood/devtools/traces/5210004321
sam: will look. if the canary is good we should roll to all nodepools but keep conservative rollout (10% -> 30% -> 100%).
eli: also add a quick perf test to the CI harness that simulates KV churn and long sequences so we don't regress this again.
maya: agreed. tagging CI owners in the ticket. closing notes: initial canary promising, hierarchical runway + KV-prefetch seems to hit p95 target without cost blowup.
